title: Free university (stronger)
question:
Some people believe that university education should be free for all students. Others think students should pay for their own studies.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Write at least 250 words.
essay:
Whether higher education should be funded by the state or by the students who benefit from it is a question that divides opinion. While there are persuasive arguments on both sides, I believe that tuition should be largely free, provided that the system is designed to reward commitment.

Those who favour charging students argue that a degree is primarily a private investment. Graduates typically earn considerably more over their lifetimes than non-graduates, so it seems reasonable that they, rather than taxpayers who may never have attended university, should bear the cost. Furthermore, fees arguably encourage students to choose their courses carefully and to take their studies seriously, since dropping out carries a financial penalty.

However, the case for free tuition is, in my view, stronger. The most compelling reason is fairness: when fees are high, talented young people from low-income families are often deterred from applying, not because they lack ability but because they fear debt. This wastes potential that society as a whole could have benefited from. In addition, the advantages of a well-educated population extend far beyond the individual graduate. Doctors, engineers and teachers trained at public expense provide services that everyone relies on, and higher earners repay the investment through income tax.

That said, completely unconditional funding may lead to some students treating university as an extended holiday. A sensible compromise would be to cover tuition for all students who maintain satisfactory progress, while withdrawing support from those who repeatedly fail modules.

In conclusion, although graduates do gain personally from their degrees, the social benefits of open access to university are so significant that the state should bear most of the cost.
